shloka_text: ततः पितामहं दृष्ट्वा वायुः पुत्रवधार्दितः । शिशुकं तं समादाय उत्तस्थौ धातुरग्रतः ।। 7.36.1 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ pitāmahaṃ dṛṣṭvā vāyuḥ putravadhārditaḥ | śiśukaṃ taṃ samādāya uttasthau dhāturagrataḥ || 7.36.1 ||
translation: ततः then, पितामहं the grandfather, दृष्ट्वा having seen, वायुः Vayu, पुत्रवधार्दितः distressed by the injury of his son, शिशुकं the child, तं that, समादाय having taken, उत्तस्थौ stood up, धातुरग्रतः in front of the creator.
explanation: Then, Vayu, distressed by the injury to his son, having seen the grandfather Brahma, picked up that child and stood up in front of the creator.
comments: Brahma revives the child, and the grateful gods each grant him boons -- Indra the name Hanuman and immunity to his thunderbolt, Surya a share of his radiance and learning, and Varuna, Yama, Kubera, Shiva, Brahma and Vishvakarma their own gifts -- grown unruly, the boy troubles the sages, who curse him to forget his strength until it is recalled -- after telling of Rkshrajas, Vali and Sugriva, Agastya completes his praise of Hanuman and the sages take their leave of Rama.

shloka_text: चलकुण्डलमौलिस्रक्तपनीयविभूषणः । पादयोर्न्यपतद्वायुस्तिस्रोपस्थाय वेधसे ।। 7.36.2 ।।
transliteration: calakuṇḍalamaulisraktapanīyavibhūṣaṇaḥ | pādayornyapatadvāyustisropasthāya vedhase || 7.36.2 ||
translation: चलकुण्डलमौलिस्रक्तपनीयविभूषणः adorned with swaying earrings, a diadem, garlands, and golden ornaments, पादयोः at the feet, न्यपतत् fell down, वायुः Vayu, तिस्रः having approached the three worlds (or times), उपस्थाय having stood before, वेधसे to the creator (Brahma).
explanation: Vayu, adorned with his moving earrings, crown, garlands, and golden ornaments, approached Brahma and prostrated himself at his feet.

shloka_text: तं तु वेदविदा तेन लम्बाभरणशोभिना । वायुमुत्थाप्य हस्तेन शिशुं तं परिमृष्टवान् ।। 7.36.3 ।।
transliteration: taṃ tu vedavidā tena lambābharaṇaśobhinā | vāyumutthāpya hastena śiśuṃ taṃ parimṛṣṭavān || 7.36.3 ||
translation: तम् him, तु indeed, वेदविदा by the knower of Vedas (Brahma), तेन by him, लम्बाभरणशोभिना shining with dangling ornaments, वायुम् Vayu, उत्थाप्य having raised up, हस्तेन with his hand, शिशुम् the child, तम् him, परिमृष्टवान् stroked.
explanation: Brahma, the knower of the Vedas and adorned with dangling ornaments, raised Vayu and then stroked the child (Hanuman) with his hand.

shloka_text: स्पृष्टमात्रस्ततः सो ऽथ सलीलं पद्मयोनिना । जलसिक्तं यथा सस्यं पुनर्जीवितमाप्तवान् ।। 7.36.4 ।।
transliteration: spṛṣṭamātrastataḥ so 'tha salīlaṃ padmayoninā | jalasiktaṃ yathā sasyaṃ punarjīvitamāptavān || 7.36.4 ||
translation: स्पृष्टमात्रः as soon as he was touched, ततः then, सः he (the child), अथ moreover, सलीलम् playfully, पद्मयोनिना by the lotus-born (Brahma), जलसिक्तम् water-sprinkled, यथा just as, सस्यम् a plant, पुनर्जीवितम् life again, आप्तवान् obtained.
explanation: As soon as the child was playfully touched by Brahma, he regained life, just like a plant revived by water.

shloka_text: प्राणवन्तमिमं दृष्ट्वा प्राणो गन्धवहो मुदा । चचार सर्वभूतेषु सन्निरुद्धं यथा पुरा ।। 7.36.5 ।।
transliteration: prāṇavantamimaṃ dṛṣṭvā prāṇo gandhavaho mudā | cacāra sarvabhūteṣu sanniruddhaṃ yathā purā || 7.36.5 ||
translation: प्राणवन्तम् alive, इमम् this (child), दृष्ट्वा having seen, प्राणः Vayu, गन्धवहः the carrier of smell, मुदा with joy, चचार moved, सर्वभूतेषु among all beings, सन्निरुद्धम् having been restrained, यथा as, पुरा before.
explanation: Seeing the child alive, Vayu, the wind god, joyfully circulated among all beings as he had done before, having previously been restrained.

shloka_text: मरुद्रोधाद्विनिर्मुक्तास्ताः प्रजा मुदिता ऽभवन् । शीतदाहविनिर्मुक्ताः पद्मिन्य इव साम्बुजाः ।। 7.36.6 ।।
transliteration: marudrodhādvinirmuktāstāḥ prajā muditā 'bhavan | śītadāhavinirmuktāḥ padminya iva sāmbujāḥ || 7.36.6 ||
translation: मरुद्रोधात् from the obstruction of Vayu, विनिर्मुक्ताः released, ताः those, प्रजाः creatures, मुदिताः joyful, अभवन् became, शीतदाहविनिर्मुक्ताः freed from cold and heat, पद्मिन्यः lotus plants, इव like, साम्बुजाः with lotuses.
explanation: Released from the obstruction of Vayu, all creatures became joyful, just like lotus plants in ponds are revived when freed from extreme cold and heat.

shloka_text: ततस्त्रियुग्मस्त्रिककुत्ऺित्रधामा त्रिदशार्चितः । उवाच देवता ब्रह्मा मारुतप्रियकाम्यया ।। 7.36.7 ।।
transliteration: tatastriyugmastrikakutऺ्itradhāmā tridaśārcitaḥ | uvāca devatā brahmā mārutapriyakāmyayā || 7.36.7 ||
translation: ततः then, त्रियुग्मः having three pairs, त्रिककुत् three-peaked, त्रिधामा having three abodes, त्रिदशार्चितः worshipped by the gods, ब्रह्मा Brahma, मारुतप्रियकाम्यया with the desire for Vayu's pleasure, देवताः to the gods, उवाच spoke.
explanation: Then, Brahma, who is associated with three pairs, three peaks, and three abodes, and is worshipped by the gods, spoke to the deities out of a desire to please Vayu.

shloka_text: भो महेन्द्रेशवरुणप्रजेश्वरधनेश्वराः । जानतामपि वः सर्वं वक्ष्यामि श्रूयतां हितम् ।। 7.36.8 ।।
transliteration: bho mahendreśavaruṇaprajeśvaradhaneśvarāḥ | jānatāmapi vaḥ sarvaṃ vakṣyāmi śrūyatāṃ hitam || 7.36.8 ||
translation: भो O, महेन्द्रेशवरुणप्रजेश्वरधनेश्वराः Mahendra, Ishvara, Varuna, Prajeshvara, Dhaneshvara, जानताम् even though knowing, अपि even, वः to you, सर्वम् all, वक्ष्यामि I shall speak, श्रूयताम् let it be heard, हितम् beneficial.
explanation: Brahma addressed the gods, including Mahendra, Ishvara, Varuna, Prajeshvara, and Dhaneshvara, stating that even though they might already know, he would speak to them about something beneficial, which they should hear.

shloka_text: अनेन शिशुना कार्यं कर्तव्यं वो भविष्यति । तद्वदध्वं वरान्सर्वे मारुतस्यास्य तुष्टये ।। 7.36.9 ।।
transliteration: anena śiśunā kāryaṃ kartavyaṃ vo bhaviṣyati | tadvadadhvaṃ varānsarve mārutasyāsya tuṣṭaye || 7.36.9 ||
translation: अनेन by this, शिशुना child, कार्यम् work, कर्तव्यम् to be done, वः for you, भविष्यति will be, तत् therefore, वदध्वम् give, वरान् boons, सर्वे all, मारुतस्य of Vayu, अस्य of this, तुष्टये for the satisfaction.
explanation: Brahma declared that this child (Hanuman) would perform a great task for them, and therefore, all the gods should grant boons to him for Vayu's satisfaction.

shloka_text: ततः सहस्रनयनः प्रीतियुक्तः शुभाननः । कुशेशयमयीं मालामुत्क्षिप्येदं वचो ऽब्रवीत् ।। 7.36.10 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ sahasranayanaḥ prītiyuktaḥ śubhānanaḥ | kuśeśayamayīṃ mālāmutkṣipyedaṃ vaco 'bravīt || 7.36.10 ||
translation: ततः then, सहस्रनयनः the thousand-eyed one, प्रीतियुक्तः filled with joy, शुभाननः having an auspicious face, कुशेशयमयीम् made of lotus flowers, मालाम् garland, उत्क्षिप्य lifting up, इदम् this, वचः word, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Then, Indra, the thousand-eyed god, filled with joy and having an auspicious face, lifted up a lotus garland and spoke these words.

shloka_text: मत्करोत्सृष्टवज्रेण हनुरस्य यथा हतः । नाम्ना वै कपिशार्दूलो भविता हनुमानिति ।। 7.36.11 ।।
transliteration: matkarotsṛṣṭavajreṇa hanurasya yathā hataḥ | nāmnā vai kapiśārdūlo bhavitā hanumāniti || 7.36.11 ||
translation: मत्करोत्सृष्टवज्रेण by the thunderbolt released from my hand, हनुः the jaw, अस्य of this, यथा as, हतः struck, नाम्ना by name, वै indeed, कपिशार्दूलः the tiger among monkeys, भविता will be, हनुमान् Hanuman, इति thus.
explanation: Indra declared that because this child's jaw was struck by the thunderbolt released from his hand, he would indeed be known by the name Hanuman, the tiger among monkeys.

shloka_text: अहमस्य प्रदास्यामि परमं वरमद्भुतम् । इतः प्रभृति वज्रस्य ममावध्यो भविष्यति ।। 7.36.12 ।।
transliteration: ahamasya pradāsyāmi paramaṃ varamadbhutam | itaḥ prabhṛti vajrasya mamāvadhyo bhaviṣyati || 7.36.12 ||
translation: अहम् I, अस्य to him, प्रदास्यामि will give, परमम् supreme, वरम् boon, अद्भुतम् wonderful, इतः प्रभृति from now on, वज्रस्य by the thunderbolt, मम by me, अवध्यः invulnerable, भविष्यति will be
explanation: I will grant him a supreme and wonderful boon: from this moment forward, he will be invulnerable to my thunderbolt.

shloka_text: मार्तण्डस्त्वब्रवीत्तत्र भगवांस्तिमिरापहः । तेजसो ऽस्य मदीयस्य ददामि शतिकां कलाम् ।। 7.36.13 ।।
transliteration: mārtaṇḍastvabravīttatra bhagavāṃstimirāpahaḥ | tejaso 'sya madīyasya dadāmi śatikāṃ kalām || 7.36.13 ||
translation: मार्तण्डः the Sun-god, तु and, अब्रवीत् spoke, तत्र there, भगवान् the revered, तिमिरापहः dispeller of darkness, तेजसः of the radiance, अस्य to him, मदीयस्य my own, ददामि I give, शतिकां a hundredth, कलाम् part
explanation: There, the revered Sun-god, dispeller of darkness, then declared, "I bestow upon him a hundredth part of my own radiance."

shloka_text: यदा तु शास्त्राण्यध्येतुं शक्तिरस्य भविष्यति । तदास्य शास्त्रं दास्यामि येन वाग्ग्मी भविष्यति ।। 7.36.14 ।।
transliteration: yadā tu śāstrāṇyadhyetuṃ śaktirasya bhaviṣyati | tadāsya śāstraṃ dāsyāmi yena vāggmī bhaviṣyati || 7.36.14 ||
translation: यदा when, तु and, शास्त्राणि scriptures, अध्येतुम् to study, शक्तिः ability, अस्य his, भविष्यति will be, तदा then, अस्य to him, शास्त्रम् knowledge, दास्यामि I will give, येन by which, वाग्ग्मी eloquent, भविष्यति he will become
explanation: And when he gains the ability to study scriptures, I will then impart knowledge to him by which he will become eloquent.

shloka_text: नचास्य भविता कश्चित्सदृशः शास्त्रदर्शने । वरुणश्च वरं प्रादान्नास्य मृत्युर्भविष्यति । वर्षायुतशतेनापि मत्पाशादुदकादपि ।। 7.36.15 ।।
transliteration: nacāsya bhavitā kaścitsadṛśaḥ śāstradarśane | varuṇaśca varaṃ prādānnāsya mṛtyurbhaviṣyati | varṣāyutaśatenāpi matpāśādudakādapi || 7.36.15 ||
translation: न च and not, अस्य to him, भविता will be, कश्चित् anyone, सदृशः equal, शास्त्रदर्शने in understanding scriptures, वरुणः Varuna, च and, वरम् boon, प्रादात् gave, न अस्य not his, मृत्युः death, भविष्यति will be, वर्षायुतशतेन अपि even by a hundred thousand years (of water), मत्पाशात् from my noose, उदकात् अपि even from water
explanation: No one will be his equal in understanding scriptures, and Varuna also granted a boon that his death will not occur even by a hundred thousand years of water, nor from Varuna's noose or from water itself.

shloka_text: यमो दण्डादवध्यत्वमरोगत्वं च नित्यशः । वरं ददामि सन्तुष्ट अविषादं च संयुगे ।। 7.36.16 ।।
transliteration: yamo daṇḍādavadhyatvamarogatvaṃ ca nityaśaḥ | varaṃ dadāmi santuṣṭa aviṣādaṃ ca saṃyuge || 7.36.16 ||
translation: यमः Yama, दण्डाद् from the mace (or punishment), अवध्यत्वम् invulnerability, अरोगत्वम् freedom from disease, च and, नित्यशः always, वरम् boon, ददामि I give, सन्तुष्टः pleased, अविषादम् freedom from dejection, च and, संयुगे in battle
explanation: Yama, being pleased, declared, "I grant him the boon of invulnerability from my mace, perpetual freedom from disease, and freedom from dejection in battle."

shloka_text: गदेयं मामिका नैनं संयुगेषु वधिष्यति । इत्येवं वरदः प्राह तदा ह्येकाक्षिपिङ्गलः ।। 7.36.17 ।।
transliteration: gadeyaṃ māmikā nainaṃ saṃyugeṣu vadhiṣyati | ityevaṃ varadaḥ prāha tadā hyekākṣipiṅgalaḥ || 7.36.17 ||
translation: गदेयं this mace, मामिका mine, न not, एनम् him, संयुगेषु in battles, वधिष्यति will kill, इति thus, एवम् in this manner, वरदः the bestower of boons, प्राह said, तदा then, हि indeed, एकाक्षिपिङ्गलः the one-eyed and tawny (Kubera).
explanation: Then, Kubera, the bestower of boons, declared that his mace would not kill this child in battles.

shloka_text: मत्तो मदायुधानां च न वध्यो ऽयं भविष्यति । इत्येवं शङ्करेणापि दत्तो ऽस्य परमो वरः ।। 7.36.18 ।।
transliteration: matto madāyudhānāṃ ca na vadhyo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati | ityevaṃ śaṅkareṇāpi datto 'sya paramo varaḥ || 7.36.18 ||
translation: मत्तः by me, मदायुधानाम् and by my weapons, च and, न not, वध्यः killable, अयम् this (one), भविष्यति will be, इति thus, एवम् in this manner, शङ्करेणापि even by Shankara, दत्तः given, अस्य to him, परमः supreme, वरः boon.
explanation: In this way, even by Shankara (Shiva), a supreme boon was granted to him, declaring that he would not be killable by Shiva or his weapons.

shloka_text: सर्वेषां ब्रह्मदण्डानामवध्यो ऽयं भविष्यति । दीर्घायुश्च महात्मा च इति ब्रह्माब्रवीद्वचः ।। 7.36.19 ।।
transliteration: sarveṣāṃ brahmadaṇḍānāmavadhyo 'yaṃ bhaviṣyati | dīrghāyuśca mahātmā ca iti brahmābravīdvacaḥ || 7.36.19 ||
translation: सर्वेषाम् of all, ब्रह्मदण्डानाम Brahma's curses/punishments, अवध्यो unkillable, अयम् this (one), भविष्यति will be, दीर्घायुश्च and long-lived, महात्मा great-souled, च and, इति thus, ब्रह्मा Brahma, अब्रवीत् spoke, वचः words.
explanation: Brahma then spoke, declaring that this child would be immune to all of Brahma's curses and would be long-lived and great-souled.

shloka_text: विश्वकर्मा च दृष्ट्वैनं बालसूर्योपमं शिशुम् । शिल्पिनां प्रवरः प्रादाद्वरमस्य महामतिः ।। 7.36.20 ।।
transliteration: viśvakarmā ca dṛṣṭvainaṃ bālasūryopamaṃ śiśum | śilpināṃ pravaraḥ prādādvaramasya mahāmatiḥ || 7.36.20 ||
translation: विश्वकर्मा Vishwakarma, च and, दृष्ट्वा having seen, एनम् him, बालसूर्योपमम् resembling the rising sun, शिशुम् the child, शिल्पिनाम् of artisans, प्रवरः the foremost, प्रादात् gave, वरम् a boon, अस्य to him, महामतिः the great-minded.
explanation: And Vishwakarma, the great-minded and foremost of artisans, having seen the child who resembled the rising sun, granted him a boon.

shloka_text: मत्कृतानि च शस्त्राणि यानि दिव्यानि संयुगे । तैरवध्यत्वमापन्नश्चिरजीवी भविष्यति ।। 7.36.21 ।।
transliteration: matkṛtāni ca śastrāṇi yāni divyāni saṃyuge | tairavadhyatvamāpannaścirajīvī bhaviṣyati || 7.36.21 ||
translation: मत्कृतानि made by me, च and, शस्त्राणि weapons, यानि which, दिव्यानि divine, संयुगे in battle, तैः by them, अवध्यत्वमापन्नः having attained invincibility, चिरजीवी long-lived, भविष्यति will be.
explanation: Vishwakarma's boon declared that the child would attain invincibility against all divine weapons made by him and would thus be long-lived.

shloka_text: ततः सुराणां तु वरैर्दृष्ट्वा ह्येनमलङ्कृतम् । चतुर्मुखस्तुष्टमना वायुमाह जगद्गुरुः ।। 7.36.22 ।।
transliteration: tataḥ surāṇāṃ tu varairdṛṣṭvā hyenamalaṅkṛtam | caturmukhastuṣṭamanā vāyumāha jagadguruḥ || 7.36.22 ||
translation: ततः then, सुराणां of the gods, तु indeed, वरैः by boons, दृष्ट्वा having seen, हि indeed, एनम् him, अलङ्कृतम् adorned/endowed, चतुर्मुखः the four-faced one (Brahma), तुष्टमनाः with a pleased mind, वायुम् to Vayu, आह said, जगद्गुरुः the preceptor of the world,
explanation: After seeing Hanuman endowed with boons from the gods, Brahma, the preceptor of the world, with a pleased mind, spoke to Vayu.

shloka_text: अमित्राणां भयकरो मित्राणामभयङ्करः । अजेयो भविता पुत्रस्तव मारुत मारुतिः ।। 7.36.23 ।।
transliteration: amitrāṇāṃ bhayakaro mitrāṇāmabhayaṅkaraḥ | ajeyo bhavitā putrastava māruta mārutiḥ || 7.36.23 ||
translation: अमित्राणां of enemies, भयकरः one who causes fear, मित्राणां of friends, अभयङ्करः one who grants fearlessness, अजेयः unconquerable, भविता will be, पुत्रः son, तव your, मारुत O Vayu, मारुतिः Maruti (Hanuman),
explanation: Brahma declared to Vayu that his son, Hanuman, would be a terror to enemies, a protector to friends, and unconquerable.

shloka_text: कामरूपः कामचारी कामगः प्लवतां वरः । भवत्यव्याहतगतिः कीर्तिमांश्च भविष्यति ।। 7.36.24 ।।
transliteration: kāmarūpaḥ kāmacārī kāmagaḥ plavatāṃ varaḥ | bhavatyavyāhatagatiḥ kīrtimāṃśca bhaviṣyati || 7.36.24 ||
translation: कामरूपः having a desired form, कामचारी moving at will, कामगः going where he desires, प्लवतां of jumpers/leapers, वरः the best, भवति will be, अव्याहतगतिः having unhindered movement, कीर्तिमांश्च and glorious/famous, भविष्यति will be,
explanation: Hanuman will possess the ability to assume any form, move anywhere at will, be the foremost among leapers, have unhindered movement, and achieve great fame.

shloka_text: रावणोत्सादनार्थानि रामप्रियकरणि च । रोमहर्षकराण्येष कर्ता कर्माणि संयुगे ।। 7.36.25 ।।
transliteration: rāvaṇotsādanārthāni rāmapriyakaraṇi ca | romaharṣakarāṇyeṣa kartā karmāṇi saṃyuge || 7.36.25 ||
translation: रावणोत्सादनार्थानि for the destruction of Ravana, रामप्रियकरणि and pleasing to Rama, च and, रोमहर्षकराणि causing hair to stand on end (awe-inspiring), एषः he (Hanuman), कर्ता will do, कर्माणि deeds, संयुगे in battle,
explanation: In battle, Hanuman will perform awe-inspiring deeds that will lead to the destruction of Ravana and be pleasing to Rama.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा तमामन्त्र्य मारुतं त्वमरैः सह । यथागतं ययुः सर्वे पितामहपुरोगमाः ।। 7.36.26 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā tamāmantrya mārutaṃ tvamaraiḥ saha | yathāgataṃ yayuḥ sarve pitāmahapurogamāḥ || 7.36.26 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, तम् him (Vayu), आमन्त्र्य having addressed/taken leave of, मारुतम् Vayu, तु indeed, अमरैः with the gods, सह together, यथागतम् as they had come, ययुः went, सर्वे all, पितामहपुरोगमाः with Brahma at the forefront,
explanation: Having spoken thus and taken leave of Vayu, all the gods, led by Brahma, returned to their respective abodes.

shloka_text: सो ऽपि गन्धवहः पुत्रं प्रगृह्य गृहमानयत् । अञ्जनायास्तमाचख्यौ वरदत्तं विनिर्गतः ।। 7.36.27 ।।
transliteration: so 'pi gandhavahaḥ putraṃ pragṛhya gṛhamānayat | añjanāyāstamācakhyau varadattaṃ vinirgataḥ || 7.36.27 ||
translation: सः he, अपि also, गन्धवहः the wind-god, पुत्रम् son, प्रगृह्य having taken, गृहम् to home, आनयत् brought, अञ्जनायाः to Anjana, तम् him, आचख्यौ informed, वरदत्तम् boon-given, विनिर्गतः having departed.
explanation: The wind-god, having taken his son, brought him home and, after departing, informed Anjana that the child was a boon.

shloka_text: प्राप्य राम वरानेष वरदानसमन्वितः । बलेनात्मनि संस्थेन सो ऽपूर्यत यथा ऽर्णवः ।। 7.36.28 ।।
transliteration: prāpya rāma varāneṣa varadānasamanvitaḥ | balenātmani saṃsthena so 'pūryata yathā 'rṇavaḥ || 7.36.28 ||
translation: राम O Rama, एषः this (Hanuman), वरान् boons, प्राप्य having obtained, वरदानसमन्वितः endowed with boons, आत्मनि in himself, संस्थेन residing, बलेन with strength, सः he, अपूर्यत was filled, यथा like, अर्णवः the ocean.
explanation: O Rama, this Hanuman, having obtained and being endowed with boons, was filled with strength residing within him, just like the ocean.

shloka_text: तरसा पूर्यमाणो ऽपि तदा वानरपुङ्गवः । आश्रमेषु महर्षीणामपराध्यति निर्भयः ।। 7.36.29 ।।
transliteration: tarasā pūryamāṇo 'pi tadā vānarapuṅgavaḥ | āśrameṣu maharṣīṇāmaparādhyati nirbhayaḥ || 7.36.29 ||
translation: तदा then, तरसा with might, पूर्यमाणः being filled, अपि even, वानरपुङ्गवः the best of monkeys, निर्भयः fearless, महर्षीणाम् of great sages, आश्रमेषु in the hermitages, अपराध्यति committed offenses.
explanation: Then, even as he was filled with immense might, the fearless best of monkeys began to commit offenses in the hermitages of the great sages.

shloka_text: स्रुग्भाण्डान्यग्निहोत्रं च वल्कलाजिनसञ्चयान् । भग्नविच्छिन्नविध्वस्तान्संशान्तानां करोत्ययम् ।। 7.36.30 ।।
transliteration: srugbhāṇḍānyagnihotraṃ ca valkalājinasañcayān | bhagnavicchinnavidhvastānsaṃśāntānāṃ karotyayam || 7.36.30 ||
translation: अयम् this (Hanuman), संशान्तानाम् of the peaceful ones, स्रुग्भाण्डानि sacrificial ladles and vessels, अग्निहोत्रम् the sacred fire, च and, वल्कलाजिनसञ्चयान् bark-garments and deer-skin collections, भग्न broken, विच्छिन्न torn, विध्वस्तान् and destroyed, करोति makes.
explanation: This Hanuman would break, tear, and destroy the sacrificial ladles, sacred fires, and collections of bark-garments and deer-skins belonging to the peaceful sages.

shloka_text: एवंविधानि कर्माणि प्रावर्तत महाबलः । सर्वेषां ब्रह्मदण्डानामवध्यः शम्भुना कृतः ।। 7.36.31 ।।
transliteration: evaṃvidhāni karmāṇi prāvartata mahābalaḥ | sarveṣāṃ brahmadaṇḍānāmavadhyaḥ śambhunā kṛtaḥ || 7.36.31 ||
translation: महाबलः the mighty one, एवंविधानि such kinds of, कर्माणि deeds, प्रावर्तत engaged in, (because) शम्भुना by Shiva, सर्वेषाम् of all, ब्रह्मदण्डानाम् curses of Brahmins, अवध्यः immune to, कृतः made (he was).
explanation: The mighty Hanuman engaged in such deeds because he had been made immune to all curses of Brahmins by Lord Shiva.

shloka_text: जानन्त ऋषयस्तं वै सहन्ते तस्य शक्तितः ।। 7.36.32 ।।
transliteration: jānanta ṛṣayastaṃ vai sahante tasya śaktitaḥ || 7.36.32 ||
translation: जानन्त knowing, ऋषयः the sages, तम् him, वै indeed, सहन्ते tolerate, तस्य his, शक्तितः due to power.
explanation: The sages, knowing his immense power, indeed tolerated his actions.

shloka_text: यथा केसरिणा त्वेष वायुना सो ऽञ्जनासुतः । प्रतिषिद्धो ऽपि मर्यादां लङ्घयत्येव वानरः ।। 7.36.33 ।।
transliteration: yathā kesariṇā tveṣa vāyunā so 'ñjanāsutaḥ | pratiṣiddho 'pi maryādāṃ laṅghayatyeva vānaraḥ || 7.36.33 ||
translation: यथा just as, केसरिणा by Kesari, तु indeed, एष this, वायुना by Vayu, सः he, अञ्जनासुतः Anjana's son, प्रतिषिद्धः forbidden, अपि even, मर्यादां the boundary, लङ्घयति transgresses, एव indeed, वानरः the monkey.
explanation: Just as this son of Anjana, though forbidden by Kesari and Vayu, indeed transgresses all limits.

shloka_text: ततो महर्षयः क्रुद्धा भृग्वङ्गिरसवंशजाः । शेपुरेनं रघुश्रेष्ठ नातिक्रुद्धातिमन्यवः ।। 7.36.34 ।।
transliteration: tato maharṣayaḥ kruddhā bhṛgvaṅgirasavaṃśajāḥ | śepurenaṃ raghuśreṣṭha nātikruddhātimanyavaḥ || 7.36.34 ||
translation: ततः then, महर्षयः the great sages, क्रुद्धाः angered, भृग्वङ्गिरसवंशजाः born in the lineage of Bhrigu and Angiras, शेपुः cursed, एनम् him, रघुश्रेष्ठ O best of Raghu's lineage, न not, अतिक्रुद्धाः excessively angry, अतिमन्यवः excessively wrathful.
explanation: Then, O best of Raghu's lineage, the great sages born in the lineage of Bhrigu and Angiras, though not excessively angry or wrathful, cursed him.

shloka_text: बाधसे यत्समाश्रित्य बलमस्मान्प्लवङ्गम । तद्दीर्घकालं वेत्तासि नास्माकं शापमोहितः । यदा ते स्मार्यते कीर्तिस्तदा ते वर्धते बलम् ।। 7.36.35 ।।
transliteration: bādhase yatsamāśritya balamasmānplavaṅgama | taddīrghakālaṃ vettāsi nāsmākaṃ śāpamohitaḥ | yadā te smāryate kīrtistadā te vardhate balam || 7.36.35 ||
translation: बाधसे you harass, यत् because, समाश्रित्य relying upon, बलम् strength, अस्मान् us, प्लवङ्गम O monkey, तत् that, दीर्घकालम् for a long time, वेत्तासि you will know (not), न not, अस्माकम् our, शापमोहितः deluded by the curse, यदा when, ते your, स्मार्यते is reminded, कीर्तिः fame, तदा then, ते your, वर्धते increases, बलम् strength.
explanation: O monkey, because you harass us relying on your strength, you will not know that strength for a long time, deluded by our curse; your strength will only increase when your fame and deeds are recalled.

shloka_text: ततस्स हृततेजौजा महर्षिवचनौजसा । एषोश्रमाणि तान्येव मृदुभावं गतो ऽचरत् ।। 7.36.36 ।।
transliteration: tatassa hṛtatejaujā maharṣivacanaujasā | eṣośramāṇi tānyeva mṛdubhāvaṃ gato 'carat || 7.36.36 ||
translation: ततः then, सः he, हृततेजौजाः having his splendor and vigor taken away, महर्षिवचनौजसा by the power of the great sages' words, एषः this (Hanuman), आश्रमाणि the hermitages, तानि those, एव indeed, मृदुभावम् a gentle state, गतः having attained, अचरत् he wandered.
explanation: Then, this Hanuman, having lost his splendor and vigor by the power of the great sages' words, attained a gentle state and wandered only in those hermitages.

shloka_text: अथर्क्षरजसो नाम वालिसुग्रीवयोः पिता । सर्ववानरराजा ऽ ऽसीत्तेजसा भास्करप्रभः ।। 7.36.37 ।।
transliteration: atharkṣarajaso nāma vālisugrīvayoḥ pitā | sarvavānararājā ' 'sīttejasā bhāskaraprabhaḥ || 7.36.37 ||
translation: अथ then, ऋक्षरजसो Ṛkṣarajas, नाम named, वालिसुग्रीवयोः of Vali and Sugriva, पिता father, सर्ववानरराजा king of all monkeys, आसीत् was, तेजसा by splendor, भास्करप्रभः radiant like the sun.
explanation: Then, there was a king named Ṛkṣarajas, the father of Vali and Sugriva, who was the king of all monkeys and shone with the radiance of the sun.

shloka_text: स तु राज्यं चिरं कृत्वा वानराणां हरीश्वरः । स च ऋक्षरजा नाम कालधर्मेण सङ्गतः ।। 7.36.38 ।।
transliteration: sa tu rājyaṃ ciraṃ kṛtvā vānarāṇāṃ harīśvaraḥ | sa ca ṛkṣarajā nāma kāladharmeṇa saṅgataḥ || 7.36.38 ||
translation: स he, तु indeed, राज्यं rule, चिरं for a long time, कृत्वा having performed, वानराणां of monkeys, हरीश्वरः the lord of monkeys, स he, च and, ऋक्षरजा Ṛkṣarajas, नाम named, कालधर्मेण by the law of time (death), सङ्गतः met.
explanation: Having ruled the kingdom of monkeys for a long time as their lord, Ṛkṣarajas eventually succumbed to the law of time.

shloka_text: तस्मिन्नस्तमिते चाथ मन्त्रिभिर्मन्त्रकोविदैः । पित्र्ये पदे कृतो वाली सुग्रीवो वालिनः पदे ।। 7.36.39 ।।
transliteration: tasminnastamite cātha mantribhirmantrakovidaiḥ | pitrye pade kṛto vālī sugrīvo vālinaḥ pade || 7.36.39 ||
translation: तस्मिन् when he, अस्तमिते had passed away, च and, अथ then, मन्त्रिभिः by the ministers, मन्त्रकोविदैः skilled in counsel, पित्र्ये in the father's, पदे position, कृतो was made, वाली Vali, सुग्रीवो Sugriva, वालिनः of Vali, पदे in the position.
explanation: After Ṛkṣarajas passed away, the wise ministers then placed Vali in his father's position, and Sugriva in Vali's position.

shloka_text: सुग्रीवेण समं त्वस्य अद्वैधं छिद्रवर्जितम् । आबाल्यं सख्यमभवदनिलस्याग्निना यथा ।। 7.36.40 ।।
transliteration: sugrīveṇa samaṃ tvasya advaidhaṃ chidravarjitam | ābālyaṃ sakhyamabhavadanilasyāgninā yathā || 7.36.40 ||
translation: सुग्रीवेण with Sugriva, समं together, तु indeed, अस्य his (Vali's), अद्वैधं undivided, छिद्रवर्जितम् without flaw, आबाल्यं from childhood, सख्यम् friendship, अभवत् existed, अनिलस्य of the wind, अग्निना with fire, यथा just as.
explanation: Indeed, his (Vali's) friendship with Sugriva was undivided and without flaw from childhood, just like the inseparable bond between wind and fire.

shloka_text: एष शापवशादेव न वेद बलमात्मनः । वालिसुग्रीवयोर्वैरं यदा राम समुत्थितम् ।। 7.36.41 ।।
transliteration: eṣa śāpavaśādeva na veda balamātmanaḥ | vālisugrīvayorvairaṃ yadā rāma samutthitam || 7.36.41 ||
translation: एष this (Sugriva), शापवशात् due to a curse, एव only, न not, वेद knows, बलम् strength, आत्मनः his own, वालिसुग्रीवयोः of Vali and Sugriva, वैरं enmity, यदा when, राम O Rama, समुत्थितम् arose.
explanation: O Rama, it was due to a curse that Sugriva did not know his own strength when the enmity between Vali and Sugriva arose.

shloka_text: न ह्येष राम सुग्रीवो भ्राम्यमाणो ऽपि वालिना ।। 7.36.42 ।।
transliteration: na hyeṣa rāma sugrīvo bhrāmyamāṇo 'pi vālinā || 7.36.42 ||
translation: न not, हि indeed, एष this, राम O Rama, सुग्रीवो Sugriva, भ्राम्यमाणो being tossed about, अपि even, वालिना by Vali.
explanation: O Rama, indeed, this Sugriva, even when being tossed about by Vali, is not the one (who is unaware of his own strength).

shloka_text: देव जानाति न ह्येष बलमात्मनि मारुतिः । ऋषिशापाहृतबलस्तदैष कपिसत्तमः ।। 7.36.43 ।।
transliteration: deva jānāti na hyeṣa balamātmani mārutiḥ | ṛṣiśāpāhṛtabalastadaiṣa kapisattamaḥ || 7.36.43 ||
translation: देव O Lord, जानाति knows, न not, हि indeed, एष this, बलम् strength, आत्मनि in himself, मारुतिः Maruta's son (Hanuman), ऋषिशाप by a sage's curse, आहृतबलः whose strength was taken away, तदा then, एष this, कपिसत्तमः best of monkeys.
explanation: O Lord, indeed, this son of Maruta (Hanuman) does not know his own strength, because he is the best of monkeys whose power was taken away by a sage's curse.

shloka_text: सिंहः कुञ्जररुद्धो वा आस्थितः सहितो रणे ।। 7.36.44 ।।
transliteration: siṃhaḥ kuñjararuddho vā āsthitaḥ sahito raṇe || 7.36.44 ||
translation: सिंहः a lion, कुञ्जररुद्धो obstructed by an elephant, वा or, आस्थितः standing, सहितो accompanied, रणे in battle.
explanation: This fragment describes a lion, either obstructed by an elephant or standing accompanied in battle, likely as part of a simile for Hanuman's strength.

shloka_text: पराक्रमोत्साहमतिप्रतापसौशील्यमाधुर्यनयानयैश्च । गाम्भीर्यचातुर्यसुवीर्यधैर्यैर्हनूमतः को ऽभ्यधिको ऽस्ति लोके ।। 7.36.45 ।।
transliteration: parākramotsāhamatipratāpasauśīlyamādhuryanayānayaiśca | gāmbhīryacāturyasuvīryadhairyairhanūmataḥ ko 'bhyadhiko 'sti loke || 7.36.45 ||
translation: पराक्रम valor, उत्साह enthusiasm, मति intelligence, प्रताप prowess, सौशील्य good conduct, माधुर्य sweetness, नय policy, अनय imprudence, च and, गाम्भीर्य profundity, चातुर्य cleverness, सुवीर्य great courage, धैर्यैः with fortitude, हनुमतः than Hanuman, कः who, अभ्यधिकः superior, अस्ति is, लोके in the world.
explanation: Who in the world is superior to Hanuman in valor, enthusiasm, intelligence, prowess, good conduct, charm, policy, imprudence, profundity, cleverness, great courage, and fortitude?

shloka_text: असौ पुनर्व्याकरणं ग्रहीष्यन्सूर्योन्मुखः प्रष्टुमना कपीन्द्रः । उद्यद्गिरेरस्तगिरिं जगाम ग्रन्थं महद्धारयनप्रमेयः ।। 7.36.46 ।।
transliteration: asau punarvyākaraṇaṃ grahīṣyansūryonmukhaḥ praṣṭumanā kapīndraḥ | udyadgirerastagiriṃ jagāma granthaṃ mahaddhārayanaprameyaḥ || 7.36.46 ||
translation: असौ this (Hanuman), पुनर moreover, व्याकरणम् grammar, ग्रहीष्यन desiring to learn, सूर्योन्मुखः facing the sun, प्रष्टुमना with a mind to ask, कपीन्द्रः king of monkeys, उद्यद्गिरेः from the rising mountain, अस्तगिरिम् to the setting mountain, जगाम went, ग्रन्थम् treatise, महत great, धारयन holding, अप्रमेयः immeasurable.
explanation: Moreover, this immeasurable king of monkeys (Hanuman), desiring to learn grammar and with a mind to question, went from the rising mountain to the setting mountain, facing the sun and bearing a great treatise.

shloka_text: ससूत्रवृत्त्यर्थपदं महार्थं ससङ्ग्रहं साद्ध्यति वै कपीन्द्रः । नह्यस्य कश्चित्सदृशो ऽस्ति शास्त्रे वैशारदे च्छन्दगतौ तथैव ।। 7.36.47 ।।
transliteration: sasūtravṛttyarthapadaṃ mahārthaṃ sasaṅgrahaṃ sāddhyati vai kapīndraḥ | nahyasya kaścitsadṛśo 'sti śāstre vaiśārade cchandagatau tathaiva || 7.36.47 ||
translation: ससूत्रवृत्त्यर्थपदं with sūtras, commentaries, meaning, and words, महार्थं of great meaning, ससङ्ग्रहं with summary, साद्ध्यति masters, वै indeed, कपीन्द्रः the chief of monkeys (Hanuman), न not, हि indeed, अस्य to him, कश्चित् anyone, सदृशः equal, अस्ति is, शास्त्रे in knowledge, वैशारदे in skill, च्छन्दगतौ in prosody, तथैव similarly.
explanation: The chief of monkeys, Hanuman, indeed masters scriptures with their aphorisms, commentaries, meanings, and words, along with their summaries, and truly, no one is his equal in knowledge, skill, or prosody.

shloka_text: सर्वासु विद्यासु तपोविधाने प्रस्पर्धते ऽयो हि गुरुं सुराणाम् । सो ऽयं नवव्याकरणार्थवेत्ता ब्रह्मा भविष्यत्यपि ते प्रसादात् ।। 7.36.48 ।।
transliteration: sarvāsu vidyāsu tapovidhāne praspardhate 'yo hi guruṃ surāṇām | so 'yaṃ navavyākaraṇārthavettā brahmā bhaviṣyatyapi te prasādāt || 7.36.48 ||
translation: सर्वासु in all, विद्यासु branches of knowledge, तपोविधाने in the practice of austerities, प्रस्पर्धते rivals, अयो he, हि indeed, गुरुं the preceptor, सुराणाम् of the gods (Brihaspati), सः he, अयं this, नवव्याकरणार्थवेत्ता knower of the nine grammars and their meanings, ब्रह्मा Brahma, भविष्यति will become, अपि even, ते your, प्रसादात् by grace.
explanation: Indeed, he rivals the preceptor of the gods (Brihaspati) in all branches of knowledge and in the practice of austerities, and this knower of the nine grammars and their meanings will even become Brahma by your grace.

shloka_text: प्रवीविवक्षोरिव सागरस्य लोकान्दिधक्षोरिव पावकस्ययुगक्षये ह्येव यथान्तकस्य हनूमतः स्थास्यति कः पुरस्तात् ।। 7.36.49 ।।
transliteration: pravīvivakṣoriva sāgarasya lokāndidhakṣoriva pāvakasyayugakṣaye hyeva yathāntakasya hanūmataḥ sthāsyati kaḥ purastāt || 7.36.49 ||
translation: प्रवीविवक्षोरिव like the ocean wishing to overflow, सागरस्य of the ocean, लोकान् worlds, दिधक्षोरिव like fire wishing to burn, पावकस्य of fire, युगक्षये at the end of an eon, हि indeed, एव certainly, यथा like, अन्तकस्य of Yama, हनूमतः of Hanuman, स्थास्यति will stand, कः who, पुरस्तात् in front.
explanation: Who indeed will be able to stand before Hanuman, who is like the ocean wishing to overflow, like fire wishing to burn the worlds, or like Yama at the end of an eon?

shloka_text: एषेव चान्ये च महाकपीन्द्राः सुग्रीवमैन्दद्विविदाः सनीलाः । सतारतारेयनलाः सरम्भास्त्वत्कारणाद्राम सुरैर्हि सृष्टाः ।। 7.36.50 ।।
transliteration: eṣeva cānye ca mahākapīndrāḥ sugrīvamaindadvividāḥ sanīlāḥ | satāratāreyanalāḥ sarambhāstvatkāraṇādrāma surairhi sṛṣṭāḥ || 7.36.50 ||
translation: एषः this one (Hanuman), एव indeed, च and, अन्ये others, च and, महाकपीन्द्राः great chiefs of monkeys, सुग्रीवमैन्दद्विविदाः Sugriva, Mainda, Dvivida, सनीलाः with Nila, सतारतारेयनलाः with Tara, Tareya, Nala, सरम्भाः with Rambha, त्वत्कारणात् for your sake, राम O Rama, सुरैः by the gods, हि indeed, सृष्टाः created.
explanation: This Hanuman, along with other great monkey chiefs like Sugriva, Mainda, Dvivida, Nila, Tara, Tareya, Nala, and Rambha, were indeed created by the gods for your sake, O Rama.

shloka_text: तदेत्कथितं सर्वं यन्मां त्वं परिपृच्छसि । हनूमतो बालभावे कर्मैतत्कथितं मया ।। 7.36.51 ।।
transliteration: tadetkathitaṃ sarvaṃ yanmāṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi | hanūmato bālabhāve karmaitatkathitaṃ mayā || 7.36.51 ||
translation: तत् that, एतत् this, कथितं has been told, सर्वं all, यत् which, मां me, त्वं you, परिपृच्छसि ask, हनूमतः of Hanuman, बालभावे in childhood, कर्म deed, एतत् this, कथितं has been told, मया by me.
explanation: All that you asked me has been told, and this deed of Hanuman in his childhood has been recounted by me.

shloka_text: श्रुत्वा ऽगस्त्यस्य कथितं रामः सौमित्रिरेव च । विस्मयं परमं जग्मुर्वानरा राक्षसैः सह ।। 7.36.52 ।।
transliteration: śrutvā 'gastyasya kathitaṃ rāmaḥ saumitrireva ca | vismayaṃ paramaṃ jagmurvānarā rākṣasaiḥ saha || 7.36.52 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, अगस्त्यस्य of Agastya, कथितम् spoken, रामः Rama, सौमित्रिः Lakshmana, एव indeed, च and, विस्मयम् wonder, परमम् great, जग्मुः attained, वानराः monkeys, राक्षसैः with Rakshasas, सह with.
explanation: Having heard what Agastya narrated, Rama, Lakshmana, and also the monkeys along with the Rakshasas, were filled with great astonishment.

shloka_text: अगस्त्यस्त्वब्रवीद्रामं सर्वमेतछ्रुतं त्वया । दृष्टः सम्भाषितश्चासि राम गच्छामहे वयम् ।। 7.36.53 ।।
transliteration: agastyastvabravīdrāmaṃ sarvametachrutaṃ tvayā | dṛṣṭaḥ sambhāṣitaścāsi rāma gacchāmahe vayam || 7.36.53 ||
translation: अगस्त्यः Agastya, तु indeed, अब्रवीत् spoke, रामम् to Rama, सर्वम् all, एतत् this, श्रुतम् heard, त्वया by you, दृष्टः seen, सम्भाषितः conversed with, च and, असि you are, राम O Rama, गच्छामहे we depart, वयम् we.
explanation: Agastya then said to Rama, "All this has been heard by you, O Rama; you have seen us and conversed with us, now we depart."

shloka_text: श्रुत्वैतद्राघवो वाक्यमगस्त्यस्योग्रतेजसः । प्राञ्जलिः प्रणतश्चापि महर्षिमिदमब्रवीत् ।। 7.36.54 ।।
transliteration: śrutvaitadrāghavo vākyamagastyasyogratejasaḥ | prāñjaliḥ praṇataścāpi maharṣimidamabravīt || 7.36.54 ||
translation: श्रुत्वा having heard, एतत् this, राघवः Rama, वाक्यम् speech, अगस्त्यस्य of Agastya, उग्रतेजसः of mighty ascetic power, प्राञ्जलिः with folded hands, प्रणतः bowed down, च and, अपि also, महर्षिम् to the great sage, इदम् this, अब्रवीत् spoke.
explanation: Having heard this speech of Agastya, who possessed mighty ascetic power, Rama, with folded hands and bowing down, spoke this to the great sage.

shloka_text: अद्य मे देवता हृष्टाः पितरः प्रपितामहाः । युष्माकं दर्शनादेव नित्यं तुष्टाः सबान्धवाः ।। 7.36.55 ।।
transliteration: adya me devatā hṛṣṭāḥ pitaraḥ prapitāmahāḥ | yuṣmākaṃ darśanādeva nityaṃ tuṣṭāḥ sabāndhavāḥ || 7.36.55 ||
translation: अद्य today, मे my, देवताः deities, हृष्टाः pleased, पितरः ancestors, प्रपितामहाः great-grandfathers, युष्माकम् your, दर्शनात् by the sight, एव only, नित्यम् always, तुष्टाः satisfied, सबान्धवाः with relatives.
explanation: Rama declared that today his deities, ancestors, and great-grandfathers, along with their relatives, were always pleased merely by the sight of Agastya.

shloka_text: विज्ञाप्यं तु ममैतद्धि यद्वदाम्यागतस्पृहः । तद्भवद्भिर्मम कृते कर्तव्यमनुकम्पया ।। 7.36.56 ।।
transliteration: vijñāpyaṃ tu mamaitaddhi yadvadāmyāgataspṛhaḥ | tadbhavadbhirmama kṛte kartavyamanukampayā || 7.36.56 ||
translation: विज्ञाप्यम् a request, तु indeed, मम my, एतत् this, हि indeed, यत् which, वदामि I speak, आगतस्पृहः eagerly, तत् that, भवद्भिः by you, मम for my, कृते sake, कर्तव्यम् should be done, अनुकम्पया with compassion.
explanation: Rama then stated that the request he was eagerly making should indeed be fulfilled by Agastya out of compassion for him.

shloka_text: पौरजानपदान्स्थाप्य स्वकार्येष्वहमागतः । क्रतूनेव करिष्यामि प्रभावाद्भवतां सताम् ।। 7.36.57 ।।
transliteration: paurajānapadānsthāpya svakāryeṣvahamāgataḥ | kratūneva kariṣyāmi prabhāvādbhavatāṃ satām || 7.36.57 ||
translation: पौरजानपदान् citizens and country-dwellers, स्थाप्य having established, स्वकार्येषु in their own duties, अहम् I, आगतः have come, क्रतून् sacrifices, एव indeed, करिष्यामि I shall perform, प्रभावात् by the power, भवताम् of you, सताम् good ones.
explanation: Having settled the citizens and country-dwellers in their respective duties, I have come here and shall indeed perform sacrifices by the power and influence of you, the virtuous ones.

shloka_text: सदस्या मम यज्ञेषु भवन्तो नित्यमेव तत् । भविष्यथ महावीर्या ममानुग्रहकाङ्क्षिणः ।। 7.36.58 ।।
transliteration: sadasyā mama yajñeṣu bhavanto nityameva tat | bhaviṣyatha mahāvīryā mamānugrahakāṅkṣiṇaḥ || 7.36.58 ||
translation: सदस्याः members of the assembly, मम my, यज्ञेषु in sacrifices, भवन्तः you, नित्यम् always, एव indeed, तत् that, भविष्यथ you shall be, महावीर्याः of great prowess, मम my, अनुग्रहकाङ्क्षिणः desiring favor.
explanation: You, who are of great prowess and desire my favor, shall always indeed be the members of the assembly in my sacrifices.

shloka_text: अहं युष्मान्समाश्रित्य तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषान् । अनुग्रहीतः पितृभिर्भविष्यामि सुनिर्वृतः ।। 7.36.59 ।।
transliteration: ahaṃ yuṣmānsamāśritya taponirdhūtakalmaṣān | anugrahītaḥ pitṛbhirbhaviṣyāmi sunirvṛtaḥ || 7.36.59 ||
translation: अहम् I, युष्मान् you, समाश्रित्य having resorted to, तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषान् whose sins are cleansed by penance, अनुग्रहीतः blessed, पितृभिः by the ancestors, भविष्यामि I shall be, सुनिर्वृतः greatly contented.
explanation: Having resorted to you, whose sins have been purified by penance, I shall be blessed by my ancestors and thus become greatly contented.

shloka_text: तदागन्तव्यमनिशं भवद्भिरिह सङ्गतैः । अगस्त्याद्यास्तु तच्छ्रुत्वा ऋषयः संशितव्रताः ।। 7.36.60 ।।
transliteration: tadāgantavyamaniśaṃ bhavadbhiriha saṅgataiḥ | agastyādyāstu tacchrutvā ṛṣayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ || 7.36.60 ||
translation: तत् therefore, आगन्तव्यम् should be come, अनिशम् constantly, भवद्भिः by you, इह here, सङ्गतैः assembled, अगस्त्याद्याः Agastya and others, तु and, तत् that, श्रुत्वा having heard, ऋषयः sages, संशितव्रताः of firm vows.
explanation: Therefore, you should constantly come here assembled together; and Agastya and other sages of firm vows, having heard that (request)...

shloka_text: एवमस्त्विति तं चोक्त्वा प्रयातुमुपचक्रमुः ।। 7.36.61 ।।
transliteration: evamastviti taṃ coktvā prayātumupacakramuḥ || 7.36.61 ||
translation: एवम् thus, अस्तु let it be, इति thus, तम् to him, च and, उक्त्वा having said, प्रयातुम् to depart, उपचक्रमुः began.
explanation: ...and having said "So be it" to him, they began to depart.

shloka_text: एवमुक्त्वा गताः सर्वे ऋषयस्ते यथागतम् । राघवश्च तमेवार्थं चिन्तयामास विस्मितः ।। 7.36.62 ।।
transliteration: evamuktvā gatāḥ sarve ṛṣayaste yathāgatam | rāghavaśca tamevārthaṃ cintayāmāsa vismitaḥ || 7.36.62 ||
translation: एवम् thus, उक्त्वा having spoken, गताः went, सर्वे all, ऋषयः sages, ते those, यथागतम् as they had come, राघवः Rama, च and, तम् that, एव indeed, अर्थम् matter, चिन्तयामास pondered, विस्मितः astonished.
explanation: Having spoken thus, all those sages departed the way they had come, and Rama, astonished, pondered over that very matter.

shloka_text: ततो ऽस्तं भास्करे याते विसृज्य नृपवानरान् । सन्ध्यामुपास्य विधिवत्तदा नरवरोत्तमः । प्रवृत्तायां रजन्यां तु सो ऽन्तःपुरचरो ऽभवत् ।। 7.36.63 ।।
transliteration: tato 'staṃ bhāskare yāte visṛjya nṛpavānarān | sandhyāmupāsya vidhivattadā naravarottamaḥ | pravṛttāyāṃ rajanyāṃ tu so 'ntaḥpuracaro 'bhavat || 7.36.63 ||
translation: ततः then, अस्तम् setting, भास्करे when the sun, याते had gone, विसृज्य having dismissed, नृपवानरान् kings and monkeys, सन्ध्याम् evening prayer, उपास्य having performed, विधिवत् according to ritual, तदा then, नरवरोत्तमः the best among men, प्रवृत्तायाम् having commenced, रजन्याम् when night, तु indeed, सः he, अन्तःपुरचरः entered the inner apartments, अभवत् became.
explanation: Then, when the sun had set, having dismissed the kings and monkeys, the best among men, Rama, performed his evening prayers according to ritual, and when night had truly begun, he entered his inner apartments. इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे वाल्मीकीये आदिकाव्ये श्रीमदुत्तरकाण्डे षट्त्रिंशः सर्गः ।। 36 ।। Thus ends the thirty-sixth sarga of Uttara Kanda of the holy Ramayana the first epic composed by sage Valmiki.
